title: Sponge, funnel, strainer, sieve (Avot 5:15)
hookLine: four kinds of students; the sieve lets the dust through and keeps the fine flour
tomorrow: Owen got in, far away. does a friendship survive that?

cards: The run-through ends. The cast sits on the edge of the stage, and the director flips open a legal pad: a whole page of notes. Four actors listen.
The first writes down every word, the jokes, the asides, the cough. The second nods at everything and has forgotten all of it by the parking lot.

The third hears one sharp note about her timing and replays it all night, while the praise slides off. The fourth listens, crosses out half, and circles two lines. So, a whole page of notes: which ones do you keep?

teach.b: Avot got there first, with kitchen tools. There are four kinds among those who sit before the sages: a sponge, a funnel, a strainer and a sieve. The sponge soaks up everything.
The funnel takes it in one end and lets it out the other.
The strainer lets the wine run out and keeps the dregs. The sieve lets the flour dust fall through and keeps the fine flour. That's the four actors.

The note-taker who keeps every cough: sponge. The nodder: funnel, the old picture of in one ear and out the other. The one replaying the single sharp note: strainer, holding on to the dregs while the wine runs away.
And the one with two circled lines: sieve. Here's the twist. The sponge sounds like the star student.
It keeps everything. But it keeps everything, the good and the grit together, and can't tell them apart. The mishnah doesn't grade the four out loud.
Readers often point to the sieve, because sifting is a skill.
Its fine flour is solet, the flour Leviticus names for offerings. Keeping isn't the goal. Choosing is.

how: Avot 5:15 is read with chapter five on summer Shabbat afternoons; in a study pair, partners often help each other sift a passage, deciding together what the main point is and what can be let go.

o: one who soaks up all they hear, good and bad
one who wipes away what others teach
one who learns fast and forgets quickly

games.q: four kinds of students — tap the pairs.
p: in one end, out the other
lets the wine go, keeps the dregs

s: the sponge is the hero of Avot's four students
a sponge soaks up the good and the grit together. readers often point to the sieve.
Avot's strainer keeps the dregs and lets the wine run out
it holds on to the worst and loses the best.
the mishnah ranks the four students from best to worst
it describes them; readers draw the lesson.

games.q: your grandmother leaves a long voice message: weather, gossip, a recipe, and one piece of advice about your sister. what does the sieve keep?
o: the advice and the recipe: the fine flour, not every word.
all of it, word for word, like a sponge; she'd want that.
the gossip about a cousin, since that's what sticks in your head.
games.why: the sieve lets the dust through and keeps the fine flour. keeping everything is the sponge; keeping the worst is the strainer.

practice: Sift today. Let three things you heard or read pass through: a headline, a comment, a passing worry, one at a time, on the out-breath.
Then keep one fine thing from the day, a kind word, a good line, a small win, and hold it for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: Sponge: the first of Avot's four students, soaking up everything at once. The sieve, last on the list, does the choosing.

orig.note: Hebrew: sponge, the first of Avot's four kinds of students.

carryVoice: Something to sift with: keep the fine flour, and let the dust fall through. Until tomorrow.
